name: implemented-by-migration-reconciliation
body:
Audit record for the implemented-by migration blocker fix (spec-review feedback-72/73/74).

INCONSISTENCY (re-verified against source, not re-derived): the pinned order — (1) rooted FQNs land, (2) branch re-scan, (3) re-point edges, (4) verify — could not execute. `apg scan` runs `layers::ingest_tree` (src/main.rs:1390) whose step 3 calls `validate_code_refs` (src/layers.rs:1580; defn 1318-1329), which bails on the first Drift (`spec drift: code FQN … is gone from the scanned graph`). After rooting, `scanned_code` holds rooted FQNs while the authored targets are still bare → the re-scan (2) aborts before the rooted graph is written. Migrating before the re-scan was refused by `layers::validate_change` (src/layers.rs:1872-1881) because the rooted destination is neither Real in `graph.jsonl` nor a declared planned node (`InvalidCodeRef`); a rename `--to` does NOT enter the planned universe — only `Record::PlannedNode` does (`apg.artifacts::code_universes_from_export`, src/artifacts.rs:1204-1210; `apg.plan_cmd::task_verb_universes`, src/plan_cmd.rs:1204-1218).

RESOLUTION [with user/coordinator — sequencing corrected; the language-rooting decision itself is unchanged and not re-litigated]: the planned-node bridge breaks the deadlock. Corrected order: (1) Language node + rooted FQNs land in code; (2) every authored target's rooted destination is declared as a planned Implementation node so `classify_code_ref` grades it Pending; (3) every `implemented-by` edge is re-pointed bare→rooted (valid as Pending, so `InvalidCodeRef` does not fire); (4) the branch re-scan realizes the planned nodes and `validate_code_refs` finds every authored target Real — no drift; (5) `apg plan verify` / the next scan confirms. Migrating before the bridge is what is forbidden, not migrating before the re-scan per se. Leaving any `implemented-by` target unrooted remains a DRIFT defect.

Applied to the three pinned nodes: requirements.requirement.language-rooting (trailing sequence sentence), requirements.requirement.implemented-by-migration (sequence paragraph rewritten to steps 1-5; data/layer framing and acceptance retained), requirements.constraint.implemented-by-migration-sequence (whole body rewritten; the DRIFT rule retained).

Also closed the solution-tier spine dead-ends: 15 `implemented-by` edges added from 11 solution components whose spine previously dead-ended (fact-cache→rust.apg.cache; delta-analyzer→rust.apg.delta; impact-closure→rust.apg.impact; db-splicer→rust.apg.splice; phase-timer→rust.apg.timing; js-ts-frontend→ts.apg-tsfrontend.scanner.collectFile + .emitNode; markdown-frontend→rust.mdfrontend + rust.mdfrontend.main; python-frontend→rust.pyfrontend + rust.pyfrontend.main; rust-manifest-discovery→the planned File node for src/rustlib/src/main.rs; language-rooting→rust.apg.graph.NodeKind.Language + rust.apg.ingest.root_module_fqn; plan-store-atomic-rewrite→apg.plan_cmd.write_through). plan-store-atomic-rewrite was the adjudicated case: its body names `write_through`, confirmed real at src/plan_cmd.rs:40-47 (the plan-store JSONL rewrite funnel), so it anchors to a real FQN. The five component bodies that stated ""carries NO implemented-by edge"" (js-ts-frontend, markdown-frontend, python-frontend, rust-manifest-discovery, language-rooting) were updated to name their planned anchors so they no longer contradict the new edges. All destinations resolve: the planned ones grade Pending, plan-store-atomic-rewrite's is Real.
